newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss 1996 chemical exports rise nominal 7.9 pct.
newsitem.headline: Swiss 1996 chemical exports rise nominal 7.9 pct.

text.p: Swiss chemical exports rose a nominal 7.9 percent in 1996 to 26.0 billion Swiss francs, the Swiss Society of Chemical Industries said. Imports increased 4.1 percent to 13.5 billion.
The overall surplus of 12.4 billion was 12 percent higher than in 1995, the industry group said in a statement.
Exports to Europe rose 7.2 percent to 16.9 billion, but went up only 6.2 percent to EU countries. Sales to eastern Europe jumped 22.8 percent and broke the billion-franc barrier.

Exports to the Americas swelled 18.0 percent to 4.2 billion, led by a 21.9 percent increase to the United States, which took in 2.3 billion francs worth of chemicals. Latin America bought 1.4 billion in chemicals, up 14.6 percent. Brazil accounted for a third of this with 500 million in imports.
Exports to Asia rose only 3.8 percent to 3.9 billion, of which Japan bought 1.4 billion, up 5.6 percent.
The European Union accounted for 85 percent of Switzerland's chemical imports.
